stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 3x - 4\). The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = f(x - 2)\). Which equation defines \(g\)?

explanation.A: Incorrect. This subtracts 2 from the output \(f(x)\); \(f(x - 2)\) replaces the input \(x\) with \(x - 2\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(f(x + 2) = 3(x + 2) - 4\); the input is \(x - 2\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This adds 2 to \(f(x)\) instead of substituting \(x - 2\) into \(f\).

verify:
x = symbols('x')
rhs = lambda s: value(s.split('=')[1])
f = 3*x - 4
g = f.subs(x, x - 2)
ok = [k for k in choices if simplify(rhs(choices[k]) - g) == 0]
assert ok == [answer]
assert simplify(g - (3*x - 10)) == 0
